body_markdown:
Most partner demand strategies were built for a buying environment that no longer exists. Buyers increasingly use AI to discover solutions, evaluate options, and inform decisions. Buying groups now dominate B2B purchases, involving on average about a dozen internal stakeholders and approaching ten external influencers. Expectations for digital experiences continue to rise.


Partner ecosystem marketing leaders who rely on traditional lead-centric approaches risk falling behind.


## **AI Is The New Front Door**


Our research and client conversations indicate that the market is changing faster than many partner demand strategies are evolving. AI is becoming a[primary gateway to information](https://www.forrester.com/report/2026-buyer-insights-buyer-usage-of-genai/RES186873) . Buyers expect relevant guidance, trusted recommendations, and seamless digital engagement. Visibility in AI-driven experiences now matters as much as visibility in traditional marketing channels.


## **The Buying Group Has Entered The Chat**


Many partner demand programs still overlook a fundamental reality: B2B buying decisions are rarely made by a single individual. Modern purchasing involves[broad buying groups](https://www.forrester.com/report/capturing-buying-group-dynamics-in-the-buying-decision-process/RES172251?ref_search=3360327_1788904894950) and extended networks of influencers. Effective partner demand efforts must account for multiple stakeholders with different priorities and information needs. Success depends on helping partners engage the entire buying group to activate opportunities rather than chasing individual leads.


## **Buyer Expectations Keep Rising**


Buyer preferences continue to evolve in ways that create new opportunities for partner ecosystems. Buyers increasingly blend self-guided and human interactions during their journey. Digital commerce options are gaining importance. Younger buyers bring consumer-like expectations for personalization, convenience, and value. These preferences favor ecosystem-led go-to-market models because partners often provide the expertise, validation, and specialized support that buyers seek throughout complex purchasing decisions.


## **Influence Has Become A Growth Engine**


Another important implication is the growing value of influence within partner ecosystems. Buyers increasingly rely on[trusted third parties](https://www.forrester.com/report/trust-is-a-hard-currency-that-suppliers-and-partners-must-leverage-now/RES182014?ref_search=3360327_1762196822704) when evaluating potential solutions. This expands the importance of partners that shape perceptions, provide expertise, and validate decisions. Organizations that invest only in transactional partner motions may miss significant opportunities to accelerate demand through influential ecosystem participants.


## **Complete Solutions Win**


The rise of complete solutions strengthens this trend. Buyers are focused on business outcomes, not individual products. Delivering those outcomes often requires multiple providers, capabilities, and services working together. Partner ecosystems are uniquely positioned to bring those elements together. Marketing leaders should evaluate how effectively their demand strategies communicate the collective value their ecosystems can provide.


## **A New Era For Partner Demand**


Partner ecosystem marketing must evolve. AI-driven discovery, complex buying groups, changing buyer preferences, and ecosystem-powered solutions are reshaping how demand is created and converted. Leaders who[update their strategies](https://www.forrester.com/report/why-ai-buying-groups-and-buyer-preferences-mandate-new-strategies-for-driving-partner-demand/RES190655?ref_search=3360327_1788967486408) now will be better positioned to help partners connect with buyers in the ways buyers increasingly prefer.
